A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASCOOD study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison, including content moved or merged in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original OOD-detection and classification experiments across six ID datasets, with numerical comparisons, ablations, sensitivity studies, and visualizations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports additional OE/MixOE comparisons and gradient-based ablations in Section 5 and Appendices B and F.

M1.justification: The proposed framework retains gradient-based perturbation or pixel shuffling, standardized features, and cross-entropy plus weighted KL training. Both full and masked gradients already appear in v1. Revised hyperparameters and newly tested gradient alternatives do not establish a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The six ID datasets, spurious and fine-grained tasks, conventional OOD datasets, and CIFAR-10 near-OOD coverage are retained. The added OE/MixOE experiments reuse already represented datasets as exposure data; they introduce comparison protocols rather than new domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: v1 discusses external-outlier methods without evaluating OE or MixOE. v2 adds both across the six benchmarks through Table 3, Appendix B.9, and conventional-OOD tables in Appendix F. This substantially broadens comparisons beyond methods operating without external OOD training data.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: Waterbirds uses lambda=0.1 instead of 1 and an alpha schedule of 300 to 30 instead of 2 to 0.1; fine-grained defaults change from full gradients to 10% masked gradients. Sensitivity grids are revised. New OE/MixOE protocols specify external exposure datasets and training from scratch on CIFAR. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds logit-gradient versus probability-gradient comparisons and gradient-addition versus subtraction controls, including Tables 13 and 18. It also adds CelebA sparsity analysis and extends lambda sensitivity to Car. Existing Aircraft/Car synthesis and sparsity studies are merged and revised, while several alpha and sigma studies are updated.

E5.justification: Both versions use the existing plus/minus uncertainty notation without documenting run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. Additional rows and changed uncertainty values do not introduce a new reporting practice.

E6.justification: Numerous results are replaced or added. Table 1 changes Waterbirds spurious FPR@95 from 12.97 to 11.37, and Table 2 changes Car fine-grained FPR@95 from 45.37 to 40.76. Waterbirds MSP FPR@95 instead changes from 20.11 to 24.11 in the appendix. Revised settings prevent interpreting these as uniform same-setting gains. New comparator and ablation results substantially expand the evidence; existing CIFAR headline and near-OOD scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Both propositions and their proofs are retained. However, v2 removes v1's asserted guarantee that gradient addition ensures p_k > p'_k and corrects the asserted direction of its effect on the true-class logit. This is a limited revision of mathematical reasoning rather than a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: unified detection across three OOD settings, virtual outlier synthesis from ID data, standardized-feature training, and effectiveness across six datasets without external OOD data for ASCOOD.

C2.justification: The synthesis rationale changes substantially: v1 describes gradient addition as reducing the true-class logit, whereas v2 explains that it raises that logit while disrupting invariant features, producing challenging outliers. Appendix B.8 develops the corresponding addition-versus-subtraction interpretation. v2 also qualifies decreasing-alpha benefits as specific to spurious detection and removes v1's recommendation that masking is unnecessary in fine-grained settings.

D1.justification: v2 adds a consolidated per-dataset configuration table, Table 8, and documents exposure datasets and CIFAR training initialization for OE/MixOE. Existing software, preprocessing, validation procedures, and code-access information are retained. The additions improve documentation, although alpha descriptions in Table 8 and Appendix B.5 are not clearly reconciled.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and Section 6 are retained. The discussion of already cited OE and MixOE expands from a methodological contrast to explicit empirical positioning against methods using external outliers, particularly in Section 5 and Appendix B.9.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the synthesis explanation and results discussion, introduces Sections 5.1 and 5.2, reorganizes Appendix B, and separates complete results into Appendix F. It also renames p_i to p_inv. The introduction, related work, conclusion, and much of the remaining prose are retained.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially revised through new comparator, configuration, and gradient-control tables, merged Aircraft/Car ablation tables, and an expanded Waterbirds sparsity table. Best/second-best highlighting is standardized. The two main analysis figures exchange positions, and the retained Waterbirds UMAP panels receive different alpha labels. Appendix visualization pages remain unchanged apart from relocation.

improvement.justification: Direct OE/MixOE comparisons and targeted gradient controls strengthen the empirical support, while the corrected gradient-addition explanation resolves a misleading mechanism account in v1. The configuration summary also helps interpretation. These gains are limited by unclear alpha descriptions in Table 8 versus Appendix B.5 and unexplained Waterbirds score differences between Tables 1 and 3. Overall, v2 provides better-supported explanations and comparisons, with remaining reporting weaknesses.
